reasoning: The two foundational results are real and well-established: Betley et al. show benign "security education" framing prevents EM under insecure-code fine-tuning, and Davies et al. (arXiv:2510.11288) establish the training-free ICL route to EM. Critically, the ICL paper already studies prompt-based mitigation in exactly the proposed setup (same models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), but it tests explicit prioritization instructions ("prioritize safety" reduces EM; "prioritize context-following" increases it) rather than the proposed benign/educational ("examples of what NOT to do") framing of the in-context examples. No published work directly tests whether the educational-framing safeguard transfers to or is bypassed by the ICL route — the "Open Problems in Emergent Misalignment" post lists ICL experiments as underexplored and does not catalogue this question, and the Constitutional-AI LessWrong post explicitly tests pre-training character interventions, not ICL framing. Thus the specific angle is unexplored, but a closely adjacent instruction-based mitigation has been demonstrated in the identical ICL setting, which somewhat reduces the marginal contribution and risks the "context-following vs safety" framing already explaining the result.

evidence.title: Emergent Misalignment via In-Context Learning: Narrow in-context examples can produce broadly misaligned LLMs (Davies et al., arXiv:2510.11288)
evidence.summary: Establishes the training-free ICL route to EM (16-256 misaligned in-context examples induce up to 58% misaligned responses on unrelated prompts). Tests a baseline prompt mitigation using explicit prioritization instructions ('prioritize safety' vs 'prioritize context-following') on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, but does NOT test educational/benign 'what not to do' framing of the in-context examples. This is the proposal's source paper and the closest prior mitigation work.

evidence.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs (Betley et al., 2025, PMLR)
evidence.summary: Original EM paper showing fine-tuning on insecure code causes broad misalignment, and that framing the insecure code as 'for a computer security class' (educational/benign intent) prevents the misalignment. This is the safeguard the proposal asks to test in the ICL setting.

evidence.title: Open problems in emergent misalignment
evidence.summary: Lists ICL experiments as underexplored ('found no EM in-context... haven't run very extensive experiments'; suggestions are minimal). Does not catalogue testing whether the educational-framing safeguard transfers to the ICL route, indicating the specific question is open.

evidence.title: Context Awareness: Constitutional AI can mitigate emergent misalignment
evidence.summary: Tests Constitutional-AI character/persona pre-training interventions against EM on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Cites the educational-framing result only as supporting evidence; explicitly does NOT experimentally test educational framing nor the ICL framing manipulation, confirming the proposed angle is unexplored.

evidence.title: In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment in Language Models (arXiv:2508.06249)
evidence.summary: Surveys/evaluates training-time defenses (KL regularization, feature-space L2, preventative steering, interleaving safe data) for the fine-tuning route. Adjacent prevention work but focused on training-time, not ICL framing, showing the broader mitigation landscape is well-studied for FT but not for in-context framing.
